messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High: possible cross-tenant KV read detected on dedicated pool - customer 915. Link: https://rbw.internal/inc/2751234567
oncall-jen: acked and paged. I'm on it. @sre-alex @sec-eli please triage
sre-alex: oncall here. what's the signal?
support-jordan: customer-ops reported 'we saw records from another tenant in response' at 11:12 UTC. They provided request id 0xabc123
sre-alex: pulling logs... running query: `select * from kvcache_access where req_id = '0xabc123'`
sre-alex: log snippets:
```
[11:12:04] pool=dedi-12 tenant=915 key=kv://model/ctx/abcd... req=0xabc123 result=OK items=1
[11:12:04] pool=dedi-12 tenant=702 key=kv://model/ctx/zzzz... req=0xabc123 result=OK items=1
```
sec-eli: those two lines look weird — same req id hitting two different tenant keys. possible routing or cache key collision.
eng-maya: checking proxy routing stack, `nginx-proxy-12` shows 11:12:03 client=10.8.5.9 -> backend dedi-12. forwarding seems normal
sre-alex: dumping kvcache metadata for key prefixes...
sre-alex: found overlapping prefix mapping: tenant 915 and tenant 702 both mapped to cache namespace `model/ctx` on node dedi-12 due to an earlier hotfix that enabled namespace aliasing
sec-eli: aliasing was supposed to be disabled for dedicated pools. this smells like config drift.
solutions-kate: customer-ops says this is sensitive - they claim PII surfaced. need escalation to SOC and account team
support-jordan: already told customer we're investigating and have paused write operations for 915
sre-alex: mitigation plan: 1) isolate node dedi-12 from serving tenant 702 (drain), 2) scrub/evict ambiguous KV namespace, 3) rotate keys if needed
oncall-jen: execute step 1 now? @eng-maya can you initiate drain and put node in maintenance?
eng-maya: starting drain: `./orchestrate drain-node --node dedi-12 --reason "isolation probe"`
incident-bot: Deploy job started: job/evict-2745
eng-maya: node dedi-12 at 35% inflight; drain expected 120s
sre-alex: while drain happens, capture heap and KV index snapshot: `s3://rbw-debug/915/2751234567/snapshot.tar.gz`
sre-alex: also grabbing tcpdump to catch cross-tenant traffic
sec-eli: SOC looped in: soc@redwood notified. starting impact matrix.
support-jordan: Can we confirm whether data that surfaced was returned to the customer or only observed in logs?
solutions-kate: customer provided screenshot of API response. it contained fields that map to tenant 702 object ids. they confirm it's persisted in their app layer.
oncall-jen: highest priority: prevent further leakage. Continue drain and put auto-failover off for the pool
eng-maya: done: node in maintenance, traffic rerouted. drain complete at 11:14:30 UTC
sre-alex: evicting KV namespace `model/ctx` from node dedi-12: `kvctl evict --node dedi-12 --prefix model/ctx`
incident-bot: Eviction completed, 3.2k keys removed
sre-alex: capturing evidence bundle and checksums. uploaded to s3 path above
sec-eli: cross-check audit logs for any reads from tenant 915 that carried data not belonging to them over the past 24h
sre-alex: initial audit: 2 reads at 11:12:04 and 11:12:05 using req ids 0xabc123 and 0xabc124. both correlate to same session
support-jordan: customer wants immediate remediation steps and timeline to full root cause
oncall-jen: draft statement to customer: short, non-technical, say we isolated the node, mitigated potential cross-tenant exposure, and are investigating root cause. CC SOC and AM
solutions-kate: I'll draft and send to account team. Also offer temporary export of customer's audit logs
sec-eli: next steps: 1) reproduce locally with namespace aliasing flag, 2) revert hotfix, 3) add automated guardrail to prevent aliasing on dedicated pools, 4) add detection rule for identical req ids across tenants
eng-maya: opening PR to remove aliasing flag default for dedicated: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/4521
sre-alex: will schedule post-incident review and notify customers impacted list
incident-bot: Pager cleared by oncall-jen
support-jordan: thanks all. handing to follow-up channel #incidents-postmortem once RCA starts
eng-maya: adding timeline notes to ticket INC-915-2751234567
sre-alex: note: no evidence of exfil beyond API response. SOC says low likelihood of mass leakage but we will confirm
sec-eli: assign to sec for RCA: sec-eli
oncall-jen: ending handoff to day team. if anything else appears ping me
customer-ops: appreciate the quick action. please keep us updated; we will escalate internally
sre-alex: last logs archived. closing real-time channel at 11:22:45 UTC
